findings.title: Findings-addressed gate's judge-leg LLM spend is recorded by no report
findings.description:
Description:
The findings-addressed gate policy makes a real LLM call inside `GateAction` — `evaluate` → `judge_residue` → `judge_residue_core` → `run_review_with_profile` (`src/squadron/review/addressed/judge.py:107`) — but that spend reaches no report. Two verified facts make this so:

1. The gate's `ActionResult.metadata` is `evidence.to_metadata()` (`policy.py:117`), and `GateEvidence` carries `judge_model`/`judge_template` but no usage/cost fields. So no `UsageRecord` is stamped under `USAGE_KEY` in run state.
2. `GATE` is not in `LLM_ACTION_TYPES` (`src/squadron/stats/usage_report.py`), so `sq stats run` does not look for a record on gate rows, and `judge_residue_core` deliberately never persists a review file, so `sq stats reviews` cannot see it either.

`run_review_with_profile` does call `resolve_cost(...)` for this judge leg (`review_client.py`), then discards the result (`JudgeLegResult` has no cost field). For a slice whose stated purpose is "report tokens, turns, time, and cost for runs and reviews," a paid LLM leg whose cost is computed and then thrown away is a silent-observability gap. This is the only verified spend path that is neither in `sq stats run` nor in `sq stats reviews`. It may be intentional scoping (the slice enumerated the four primary LLM actions), but the incidental `resolve_cost` call that gets discarded argues it wasn't a clean "we don't track gates" decision. Worth confirming: either record the judge leg via `UsageCapture` (it has the `ActionContext`, so `context.usage_capture` is available), or drop the `resolve_cost` call in that path to avoid implying it is priced.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews` can't recover the alias, so a subscription cost's basis label disagrees with `sq stats run`
findings.description:
Description:
`_record` derives `record.alias` as `requestedModel if requestedModel in get_all_aliases() else None`. But `requestedModel` frontmatter holds the resolved *model id* (`review_client.py` sets `result.requested_model = resolved_model`, where `resolved_model` is a model id, not the alias name), and that key is only written at all when the model was substituted (`persistence.py:459`). So `requestedModel in get_all_aliases()` is essentially always false → `record.alias` is ~always `None` in the reviews view.

The cost *number* is still correct in both views (it is stored in frontmatter as `costUsd`/`costBasis`), so this only affects `cost_cell`'s subscription override in `src/squadron/cli/stats_views.py` (`_is_subscription(record.alias)`): the same subscription-tier spend shows as `$X api-rate equiv.` in `sq stats run` (where the record carries the alias name) but `$X prov` in `sq stats reviews`. Narrow and cosmetic, but it is a cross-view inconsistency in cost-basis labeling for a cost-reporting feature. If the label matters, the alias *name* (not the model id) would need to be persisted to the artifact frontmatter.

findings.title: `cost_cell` re-reads the alias table from disk once per rendered row
findings.description:
Description:
`_is_subscription` calls `get_all_aliases()`, which re-parses both `data/models.toml` and `~/.config/squadron/models.toml` on every call (no `lru_cache`/`cache` in `src/squadron/models/aliases.py`). In the table render, `cost_cell` is invoked per row (`_usage_cells`), so `sq stats run` over a large run does O(rows) redundant TOML reads. This is a CLI/report path, not a hot loop, so impact is minor, but it is cheap to hoist: read the alias table once and pass it in (the tests already patch `stats_views.get_all_aliases`, so a single call site is easy to keep correct).

findings.title: SDK session/agent telemetry folding and error-path capture are correct
findings.description:
Description:
Verified the riskiest mechanic end to end. `SDKExecutionSession.dispatch` now returns `SessionReply` and sets `exc.telemetry = turns.telemetry.snapshot()` on `ProviderError` while keeping the `finally` bookkeeping intact; `_read_turn` folds an `is_error` result before raising (`accept_error=False`) and relies on `collect` to fold it on the interrupt drain (`accept_error=True`), so a stalled turn's drained spend is captured exactly once. `DispatchTurns.fold_result` warns once per dispatch when a result reported no usage. `ClaudeSDKAgent` stamps `TURNS_KEY`/`USAGE_KEY`/`COST_USD_KEY` on the final translated message and attaches the call's telemetry snapshot to any `ProviderError` it re-raises (leaving an already-set telemetry intact). The `usage_capture` module centralizes record construction, `resolve_cost` precedence, and the "nothing reported → no record" guard, and the executor threads one `UsageCapture` per run to every step executor including fan-out (`sdk_session=None` but capture preserved). The `SessionReply`/`compact`/`capture_summary` signature changes are consistently propagated through all call sites and tests. This is well-tested with behavior-level assertions (`test_dispatch_usage.py`, `test_usage_capture.py`, `test_state_usage.py`, `test_sdk_session.py`), including cancellation-propagates-without-record, partial-stall, once-per-run pricing warnings, and the state round-trip.
